items.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998
items.q: Ebony came, I think it was Ebony, and they took pictures of us.

ctx.x: I’ll take that as a yes.

Yes. They introduce me on the radio, “And now we have Etta James” and the people in the front row say “Jones, Jones” you know, they’d be telling. But it happens to her also. She was working in San Francisco and somebody hollered “Don’t Go To Strangers.” And she said, “Oh, did you come to see Etta Jones? I’m so sorry, because I’m the other one.” So she had a little speech that she used to say, about she sings this way, and she sings the soft stuff, and I sing the other. Something like that. I don’t know exactly,…
How long ago was that? © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
